CITY OF AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  City Hall Council Chambers ∙ 410 Avalon Canyon Road, Avalon, CA
  Regular Meeting – March 21, 2023 at 5:00 p.m.

This meeting is viewable in person at the Council Chambers or via livestream:

  Facebook: (http://www.facebook.com/CityOfAvalonOfficial)
  YouTube (http://www.youtube.com/cityofavalonca)
  Website (http://www.cityofavalon.com/meetings)
  Cable (Catalina Broadband Solutions Channel 3)

The Council Chambers can accommodate a maximum of 30 participants, at which point the general
public may address the Planning Commission on an agenda item by waiting in the City Hall Court
Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time. No one will be admitted into the Council Chambers
who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. The Planning Commission is not accepting live
comments electronically at this time.

The public can submit written comments prior to 3:00 p.m. 7 days prior to the meeting in person
to the Planning Department at City Hall or via email to dromo@cityofavalon.com.

Staff reports for each agenda item are posted a minimum of 72 hours prior to the meeting and are
available for review in person or on the City website at http://www.cityofavalon.com.

  In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
  meeting, please contact the City Clerk’s office (310) 510-0220 ext. 119. Notification 48 hours prior to the
  meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28
  CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are
  available for the public inspection at the time the records are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members
  of the Planning Commission. Such records shall be available at City Hall located at 410 Avalon Canyon
  Road.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE/ROLL CALL

ORAL COMMUNICATION: This is the time for any member of the public to address the
Planning Commission on any matter not on the agenda that is within the subject matter jurisdiction
of the City. The Brown Act, with limited exceptions, does not allow the Commission or staff to
discuss or take action on issues brought forth under Public Comment. Concerns may be referred
to staff or placed on the next available agenda. Please note that comments from the public will
also be taken on each agenda item. Comments shall be limited to three minutes per person.

CONSENT CALENDAR: All items listed under the Consent Agenda are considered to be routine
in nature and will be approved by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items

must file a written appeal, and include an appeal fee of $1027.00 with the City Clerk within fifteen
(15) calendar days of such action. Any person challenging actions of the Planning Commission
may be limited to issues he or someone else raises in writing prior to or orally at the hearing. Any

   PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 21, 2023
  STAFF REPORT – PC# 2835
  RESOLUTION # 23-08

Item No. ____ – Public Hearing

Submitted by: Donna Terpinitz-Romo, Planning Senior Administrative Assistant

BACKGROUND

Project Title: Application for a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit
located at 304 Clemente Avenue.

Project Description:

Request for approval of a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit to allow the
renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration located within a single family residence. The unit consists of two (2) bedrooms and two
(2) bathrooms. The project is in the Coastal Zone and subject to a Coastal Development Permit,
which requires a public hearing and Planning Commission approval. The Planning Commission
will determine whether the project is within the 300-foot appealable seaward area boundary.
The project is Categorically Exempt under Section 15305 of the State CEQA Guidelines – Minor
Alterations in Land Use Limitations.

  Owner/Applicant:  Ronald and Cora’lee Carolla
  ADDRESS:  304 Clemente Avenue
  APN:  7480-038-089
  Zone:  Medium Density Residential

Page 1 of 20
 Location Map:

The Avalon Municipal Code (“AMC”) § 3-1.310(e)(5) provides that the Planning Commission
shall consider, “whether granting the Transient Rental License shall result in any year round
residence located adjacent to the proposed transient rental having more than a majority of the
adjacent residences permitted or licensed for transient rental use.

Page 2 of 20
 Saturation:

AMC § 3-1.310(e)(5) provides that the Planning Commission shall consider, “whether granting
the Transient Rental License shall result in any year round residence located adjacent to the
proposed transient rental having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or
licensed for transient rental use…”. Upon analysis, the saturation map below indicates that less
than 50 % of the properties adjacent to 28 Avalon Terrace Road (28 Sol Vista) hold either
conditional use permits or Transient Rental licenses.

Floor Plan

The property is of ample size for a Transient Rental. The property is located at the base of a
mountain with close proximity to the main street in Avalon. The property consists of (2) two
bedrooms and (2) bathrooms located on the second story of the house. The living space, dining
room, kitchen, laundry room and bathroom is on the first story.
Page 3 of 20
 Property Manager/24 Hour Contact: The property Manager is Veronica Bravo
Phone Number: 310-562-6028

GROWTH POLICY

Southern California Edison (SCE) has determined the conversion to a transient rental will not
require a water allocation; thus, the application is in compliance with the 2023 Growth Policy.

CEQA REVIEW

The proposed project is Categorically Exempt under Section 15305 of the State CEQA
Guidelines - Minor Alterations in Land Use Limitations (i.e., CUP for transient rental) which do
not result in changes in land use or density.

DISCUSSION

The proposed project involves a request of approval of a transient rental license under Article
3 of the AMC. Transient rental use is permitted in any zone upon Planning Commission
approval of a Transient Rental License. (AMC 9-6.602(a)) The house has been previously used
as a vacation home.

COASTAL DEVELOPMENT PERMIT:

In December 2016, the City received an opinion letter from the California Coastal Commission
(Coastal Commission) noting their position that conversion to transient use constitutes a
change in intensity in use and should be authorized pursuant to a coastal development permit.
Based on the opinion, the application for transient rental use must include a Coastal
Development Permit (CDP).

The project is in the Coastal Zone and is subject to a Coastal Development Permit, which
requires a public hearing and Planning Commission approval. Specifically, the project requires
a Coastal Development Permit under Section 9-8.102(b)(2)(v) of the AMC, as the proposed
project seeks to allow the renting or leasing of a room or rooms with or without table boards
for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration (Transient Rental – Section 9-
6.602 (a) of the AMC) at 304 Clemente Ave.

Page 4 of 20
 Under AMC 9-8.103(h), the Planning Commission must determine whether the project is
within the 300-foot appealable area boundary. Based on the appealable area map excerpt
included below, it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission make the finding
that the project is within the 300-foot appealable zone.

An appeal of the Planning Commission’s Coastal Development Permit action may be filed with
the City Council within fifteen (15) days after mailed notice of the action to the applicant. Any
person may appeal the Planning Commission’s determination that a proposed project is
seaward of the appealable seaward area boundary to the Coastal Commission, and following
exhaustion of local appeals, any aggrieved person may appeal actions on local Coastal
Development Permits seaward of the appealable area boundary to the Coastal Commission.

The proposed change in use conforms to the certified Local Coastal Plan (AMC 9-8.103(d) (1))
because it increases access of the public to the coastal zone. For the Planning Commission to
issue a Coastal Development Permit, the Avalon Municipal Code requires that the Planning
Commission make certain findings. These findings and corresponding explanations of the
project’s compliance are as follows:

(1)  The use is consistent with the goals and objectives of the public access and recreation
policies of the California Coastal Act.

The Coastal Commission opinion letter noted that vacation rentals in the coastal zone are seen
as providing access to coastal areas and complies with the intent of the California Coastal Act.

(2)  The use is in conformance with the Certified Local Coastal Program for the City of
Avalon, which includes the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal Plan for Avalon, as well as
the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances.

Transient rental use is allowed in any zone with a Transient Rental License, it is supported
(with appropriate restrictions) by the Coastal Commission and the LCP. The change in use
complies with the Affordable Housing Ordinance because this does not involve an affordable
housing project or unit (AMC 9-11.107).

Page 5 of 20
 (3)  The use has received all necessary local approvals issuable by the Planning
Commission, including Growth Ordinance Pre-Approved (in concept) together with water
allocation, as may be required.

The change in use is not considered growth and is not subject to the Growth Ordinance and SCE
has determined that the change in use does not require an additional water allocation. The
Commission had determined that limiting occupancy to two (2) per bedroom plus additional
two (2) occupancy during any stage of fresh water restrictions is appropriate. The only local
approval issuable by the Planning Commission that is applicable to the project is the requested
Coastal Development Permit and Transient Rental License.

The application is allowed under the 2023 Growth Policy.

(4)  The use has been cleared with respect to environmental regulations of CEQA, as
necessary.

The proposed use is categorically exempt under CEQA Section 15305 of the State CEQA
Guidelines – Minor Alteration in Land Use Limitations (i.e., CUP for transient rental) which
does not result in change in land use and density. Further, this project has no potential to
cause a significant effect on the environment because it will approve transient rental use for
just a single property. (14 CCR §15061(b)(3))

(5)  For all development seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, the
proposed development conforms to the public access and recreation policies of Chapter 3 of
the Coastal Act.

The project is not located seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, and is
consistent with Chapter 3 of the Coastal Act, as stated in the opinion letter referenced above,
because the rental use promotes public access to the coast.

TRANSIENT RENTAL LICENSE

In order to approve the requested Transient Rental License, the Planning Commission must
make three (3) specific findings as required by Section 3-1.310(b) (1-3) of the AMC. These
findings and corresponding explanations of the project’s compliance with these findings are as
follows:

(1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings, and structures
shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where such use
will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses, buildings, and
structures.

The subject property and all surrounding properties are developed with single and multi-unit
residential units. The requested Transient Rental License does not involve any physical changes
to the existing residence that would adversely affect or be materially detrimental to adjacent

Page 6 of 20
 uses, buildings, and structures.

(2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape to
accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping, and other
development features prescribed in this chapter or as required as a condition in order to
integrate said use with the uses in the neighborhood.

The requested Transient Rental License does not involve any changes to the existing
improvements on the subject property, and the transient use has such improvements as to
integrate properly in the neighborhood.

(3)  The site on which the transient rental use is located is served by a street that is
adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of traffic that
such use would generate.

The requested Transient Rental License will allow transient rental use of an existing residence
that is served by an improved street adequately designed to serve the property.

In addition to the above findings, which apply to all Transient Rental Licenses, Section 3-
1.310(e)(1-6) of the AMC requires the Planning Commission to consider six (6) additional factors
prior to taking action on applications for the transient rental license for transient rental
housing. The applicable factors and corresponding explanations of how they relate to the
requested transient rental license are as follows:

(1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed by
the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has been
rented for periods of more than thirty (30) consecutive days to the same occupant at any time
during the two (2) years preceding the application.

The Transient Rental Housing Impact Statement submitted by the applicant indicates that the
property has been used as a home by the owner and has not been rented for periods of more
than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at any time in the prior two years.

(2) Neighborhood Impacts. The Planning Commission shall consider the objections of the
owners and occupants of neighboring properties in determining whether the proposed
transient rental use is consistent with the surrounding properties and the extent to which such
impacts may be mitigated by the imposition of the standard conditions listed below or by the
imposition of additional conditions. The Planning Commission may consider objections
previously made in connection with applications for transient rental use at other properties
located within the same general area as the subject application; however, the Planning
Commission should consider the time between the prior application and the subject
application, the geographic proximity of the subject application to the prior application, any
differing circumstances, and additional mitigating measures proposed by the applicant, and
changes in the general area, in determining the weight to be given such prior objections.

Page 7 of 20
 There have been no opposing comments or letters.

(3) Single- and Multiple-Unit Properties. In the absence of other negative findings, (a) where
the property is the only unit owned by the applicant in the City and the applicant proposes to
use the property himself from time to time; or (b) where the subject property contains
multiple units, and those other units are utilized for year round rental or occupancy, or the
applicant owns other separate properties in the City of Avalon which are utilized for year-
round rental or occupancy, the Planning Commission should approve the application.

The house has been owner occupied and has not been rented out for periods over 30 days to
the same person.

(4) Condominium Associations Having Ten (10) or More Units. In the case of an application
concerning property located within a condominium or similar congregate housing project
consisting of ten (10) or more units, the applicant shall be required to demonstrate that any
governing body of the subject association generally allows transient rental uses at the
condominium or congregated housing project.

There are less than 10 units in this complex.

(5)  The Planning Commission shall consider whether granting the Transient Rental License
shall result in any year round residence located adjacent to the proposed transient rental
having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or licensed for transient
rental use. "Adjacent" means having a common property line with the proposed transient
rental unit except for the existence of a public street or alley.

Upon analysis, the saturation map on page three (3) indicates that less than 50% of properties
at this Complex currently hold active CUPs or Transient Rental Licenses. Thus, there will not be
a majority of adjacent residences permitted or licensed for transient rental use.

(6) The total square footage of the dwelling unit and the size of each bedroom shall be
considered for determining whether to grant the Transient Rental License.
The property is of ample size for a Transient Rental. The property is located in the flats with
close proximity to the main street in Avalon. The property consists of (2) two bedrooms and (2)
bathrooms located on the second story of the house. The living space, dining room, kitchen,
laundry room and bathroom on the first story.

RECOMMENDATION

Based on the preceding discussion of the proposed project’s compliance with the applicable
principles and standards of the Avalon Municipal Code, the proposed use will not jeopardize,
adversely affect, endanger, or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety, or

Page 8 of 20
 general welfare, or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
vicinity of such use. Therefore, staff recommends the Planning Commission:

  1. Find the project categorically exempt under Section 15305 of the State CEQA Guidelines;
  2. Adopt the findings necessary to support approval of the Coastal Development Permit,
  including that the project is within the 300-foot appealable zone;
  3. Adopt the findings necessary to approve the transient rental license ; and
  4. Find that the application is allowed under the 2023 Growth Policy.
  5. Adopt Resolution No. PC 23-08

 SUMMARY
Immersive Education LLC (dba “Akuario”) has agreed to lease a ~1,288ft2 space on the southern
edge of the Island Plaza location (209 Catalina Ave, Avalon, 90704) from the Catalina Island
Company. The initial lease is for a period of six months beginning July 2023, with a view to
annual extensions thereafter. The space is bounded on three sides by wooden peeler poles and
by chain link fencing associated with the Golf Gardens mini golf course on the southern side
(see Figure 1). The space is currently occupied by picnic tables. Akuario plans to install a
cylindrical (22’ wide x 16’ high) dome theater showcasing immersive underwater films. The
proposed opening date for the experience is 1 July 2023. To meet this deadline, initial site
development and light construction is required beginning in May 2023.

THE EXPERIENCE
Visitors will be encouraged to purchase tickets in advance through a ticketing system
installed at the Long Beach Ferry Terminal, but walk-ups will be welcomed. After a short (~5
min) wait inside of the line management system, visitors will be escorted into the theater and
seated on a first-come, first-served basis. The content will be projected from a single 12,000
lumen projector in the center of the theater onto the dome screen. The experience duration is
30 minutes, with two shows per hour. We initially plan to operate for eight hours per day, with
tentative business hours of 1pm-9pm. These hours may be extended during peak season,
consistent with the operating hours of neighboring businesses.

  i)  Contact an underground utility surveying company in advance of any groundwork.
  ii)  Expand the eastern edge of the peeler pole fence to match the width of the western
  edge of the peeler pole fence (see Fig 1, attached). Holes in the asphalt will be
  patched or used for ground anchoring of the proposed deck (see iv) below).
  iii)  Install a lockable electrical sub-panel on the southeast corner of the proposed
  location. Power will be taken from the mini golf course office building panel.
  iv)  Install anchoring for the deck/dome through the asphalt into the ground below, to

  v)  Install a rectangular 23’ x 25’ wooden deck (~5” high) within the revised footprint of

  located on the easternmost side of the location, and a 5’ long ADA compliant ramp
  (1:12 slope) will be installed on the western edge of the deck.
  vi)  Assemble the 22’ wide frame of the structure centered on, and attached to, the deck.
  vii)  Install a 20’ wide fiberglass dome at a 20-degree angle on top of the frame using a
  telehandler or similar (see Figure 2 – exterior cover not shown).
  viii)  Install an all-weather, fire retardant, printed vinyl cover attached to the exterior of
  the structure.

1|Page  9 March 2023
 FIRE CODE CONSIDERATIONS
  i)  Maximum capacity of 22 people (20 audience, 2 staff – see attached preliminary
  seating plan, Figure 3).
  ii)  Two means of entry/egress spaced no less than half of the diagonal of the interior
  space (=10ft) to be provided (center to center).
  iii)  One 5lb A/B/C type fire extinguisher to be installed with high visibility signage in
  between the two doors. Extinguisher will be regularly inspected (records kept) and
  undergo annual inspection by the local fire department.
  iv)  Self-illuminating fire exit signs above each door.
  v)  Seating will be either row seating with fixed cushions and tiltable backs, or
  individual cushioned chairs with reclined backs. All seating will be fixed to the floor.
  A removable seat may be used in the ADA compliant space at the front.
  a. Row spacing no less than 12”
  b. No more than four seats per row
  c. At least 18” width per person

ADA COMPLIANCE CONSIDERATIONS
  i)  The exterior deck ramp will have a slope of no greater than 12:1; no handrails
  required.
  ii)  Doors will be 32” or wider, with no greater than a 1/4” rise when entering the
  structure.
  iii)  The narrowest interior space will be 32” for no more than a 24” distance and will be
  36” throughout elsewhere.
  iv)  One ADA compliant space (36” wide x 48” deep) with an associated companion seat
  will be reservable upon booking. The ADA space may be used for general seating
  when the ADA space has not been reserved.

INTERIOR FINISHING
  i)  Floors and walls will be carpeted using office-style carpeting.
  ii)  Round, recessed wall-mount speakers will be installed around the perimeter of the
  theater.
  iii)  A fake rock structure decorated with “corals” and other underwater elements will be
  installed to disguise the projector truss/assembly. The structure will be created
  using painted open cell spray foam insulation (commonly used in residential and
  commercial applications) over an interior metal framework, attached to the floor
  below. A dedicated fan and vent slots will be installed as part of the structure to
  allow for adequate airflow to/from the projector.

2|Page  9 March 2023
 OTHER CONSIDERATIONS
  i)  Traffic: Given that the location is within an active tour bus terminal, special
  attention will be paid to traffic safety issues, in particular pedestrians
  entering/exiting IMMERSED.
  a. An existing crosswalk between the tour bus ticket booth and the picnic area is
  in place and will serve as the main point of entry/exit to IMMERSED – this will be
  repainted to enhance visibility.
  b. Line management will occur within the peeler pole fence to reduce overflow into
  the plaza. Waiting outside of the peeler pole boundary will not be permitted and
  will be actively monitored by staff.
  ii)  Lighting: operation during summer months will likely extend into the evening and
  nighttime.
  a. Sufficient exterior lighting will be provided for the evening operations, achieved
  through a combination of deck mounted floodlights and solar powered
  stanchion lights. Additional lighting may be installed on the chain link fence as
  needed.
  iii)  Noise:
  a. To comply with City noise ordinance, construction activities will not occur from
  7pm to 8am, or anytime on Sundays.
  b. During general business operation, sound levels will be maintained to less than
  60dB as measured at a distance of 150ft away. Primary sources of noise will be
  the amplified soundtrack playing inside the dome (dampened by the walls, floor,
  carpeting, exterior structure), an external blower for an 18,000BTU HVAC system
  (~30dB), and a small blower for the inflatable portion of the dome cover.
